title: Every filter was rejected under a binding day limit; the limit no longer binds, so the low-edge money needs re-testing under the 05:15-10:00 window
claim: About 70% of the money goes on backs with expected CLV under 6%, which realised roughly zero, and every attempt to cut them (6% bar, top-up bars, drift filters) lost only because the freed GBP4,000 budget flowed to later, worse races. Since the 10:00 stop (5 Nov) the day limit was not reached on 5 of 6 days (GBP3,934.82, 2,942.70, 3,999.99, 2,474.27, 2,074.63, 1,789.84), so that displacement argument no longer holds and those tests are stale.
evidence: Ledger review-1020: fills 10-20 Oct by expected CLV - 3-3.5% realised -0.3% on GBP11,117, 3.5-4% -1.1%, 4-5% +1.2%, 5-6% +0.4%, 6-8% +3.8%, 10-15% +14.8%, 15-25% +35.7%, 25%+ +56.2%; 'the closing model's small edges (3-6% expected closes level, 70% of the money)'. Ledger rule-candidates-replay-1020 verdict: 'under the binding day limit each filter takes out bets that close about level and the budget goes on later, worse ones'. Ledger topups-1020: top-ups at expected CLV under 6% GBP21,806 at -1.2%. Day stakes: TRADING.md lines 1707-1708, 1721-1722, 1734-1735, 1745-1746, 1755-1756, 1768-1769. Ledger removal-tilt-replay-1109: served rule averaged GBP2,986 a day staked against the GBP4,000 limit - 'what is on offer at the bar, not the limit or the selection, is what binds'. Config: trading/config_live.json clv_bar 0.03, trade_until 10:00.
why_it_matters: If the 3-4% bucket still realises about -0.3% to -1.1% after cuts, it is a pure drag now that nothing better is displaced; size not measured for 22 Oct - 10 Nov (the calibration table exists only for 10-20 Oct, at a different rule).
test_design: 1) Descriptive first (no rule fitted): rerun the review_1020.py calibration on live fills 22 Oct - 10 Nov from live_orders joined to betfair_live_marks final BSP, CLV after reduction factors, by expected-CLV bin x first back/top-up. 2) Register in reports/research_ledger.jsonl before the run, then replay through research/queries/done/replay_1108.py machinery with config_live.json as it stands (05:15-10:00, ladder, cap 5): arms clv_bar 0.04 and 0.05 for top-ups only, and for all backs. Measure: daily CLV x stake after reduction factors, arm minus served, same day. Pass: positive sum, 90% day-bootstrap interval of the mean daily difference above zero, deflated Sharpe >= 0.95 (research/overfit.py) with all bar variants ever tried counted (at least the 6%, 5% top-up, nr-bar 3%/5% and these). Needs 30+ replay days (available from 12 Oct).

checks.reason:
Every cited number checks out, but the central inference ("lost ONLY because of displacement", "pure drag now") is overstated and one later test on the current window contradicts it.

CONFIRMED
- reports/research_ledger.jsonl line 409 (review-1020): calibration 10-20 Oct quoted exactly (3-3.5% -0.3% on GBP11,117; 3.5-4% -1.1%; 4-5% +1.2%; 5-6% +0.4%; 6-8% +3.8%; 10-15% +14.8%; 15-25% +35.7%; 25%+ +56.2%) and "3-6% expected closes level, 70% of the money". research/queries/done/rule_candidates_replay_1020.py:8-9 gives the 3-6% money as GBP29,114. The CLV there is per fill scaled by settled/matched price (research/queries/done/review_1020.py:77), i.e. after the cuts.
- Line 410 (rule-candidates-replay-1020) verdict and line 403 (topups-1020, under 6%: GBP21,806 at -1.2%) quoted exactly. The "5% top-up bar" is real: line 378 (stake-per-horse-1016, "worse - the limit spent later on more horses").
- Day stakes: TRADING.md:1708 GBP3,934.82, :1722 GBP2,942.70, :1735 GBP3,999.99 (limit reached 09:30 UK, :1731), :1746 GBP2,474.27, :1756 GBP2,074.63, :1768 GBP1,789.84. Limit not reached on 5 of 6 days is correct (5 Nov was GBP65.18 short and still topping up at 10:00:02).
- Line 650 (removal-tilt-replay-1109): "served rule averaged GBP2,986 a day staked against the GBP4,000 limit" quoted exactly. trading/config_live.json:5 clv_bar 0.03, :18 trade_until 10:00.
- No flat 4%/5% bar has been run on the 10:00 window: research/arms/run.py:42-46 holds only rising-bar arms (bar_slope 0.01/0.02), stop0900 and top-up caps; no ledger entry after 5 Nov tests a bar. The live code has one bar for first backs and top-ups (trading/strategy.py:182, trading/session.py:329), so a top-up-only bar exists only as a replay policy (blend_ladder_replay_1020.py:256 topup_bar).

NOT SUPPORTED / OVERSTATED
1. "Every attempt lost only because the freed budget flowed to later, worse races" holds for the 16 and 20 Oct replays, not for the later ones, which lost while staking LESS:
 - replay-nr-bar-1021 (line 427): a uniform bar raise (3%/5% after the expected cut) lost GBP231 / GBP182 CLV x stake after reductions with GBP3,078 / GBP8,365 less staked, limit reached on 4 days not 9 - "it drops good backs with the bad".
 - arms-full-1103 (line 569; TRADING.md:1796-1798): bar rising 1%/hour GBP5,766 and 2%/hour GBP5,402 against the rule's GBP6,101, "higher CLV ... on much less money"; stop at 09:00 GBP5,457; "nothing earns more by backing less".
 - removal-tilt-replay-1109 (line 650) is itself a test in the non-binding regime (trade_until 10:00, GBP2,986 a day): dropping the thinnest-edge third cost GBP1,444.32 with GBP29,143 less staked and nothing redeployed (my arithmetic: the dropped money earned about +5.0% after the cuts) - "those markets still add money ... no further filter of this kind". So the premise that low-edge money is a drag once displacement is gone has already failed once on the current window, for a different selector.
 - removal-by-market-1109 (line 648): the rule's runners with no removal to come +3.40% after the cut on GBP308,920 (2 Oct - 8 Nov).
2. The "roughly zero" calibration is 11 days at an older rule: before the guard, ladder and max price 200 (21 Oct), the cap of 5 top-ups (22 Oct) and the sectionals blend (24 Oct). Not measured since. In pounds it is small: GBP11,117 x -0.3% is about -GBP33 over 11 days, and the 4-5% and 5-6% bins were positive, so a 5% bar removes a positive bin on that same table.
3. Test design error: the replay_1108.py machinery hard-codes cfg.trade_from = '06:15' (blend_ladder_replay_1020.py:51, kept at replay_1108.py:20-22), so it replays 06:15-10:00, not "config_live.json as it stands (05:15-10:00)"; the override must be removed for the GMT days (25 Oct on).
4. The trial count for the deflated Sharpe is at least 14, not about 6: 5% top-up bar (1016), top-ups 6% and blend+ladder+6% (blend-ladder-1020), bar 6%, short bar, no drift, 6%+no drift (rule-candidates-1020), nr-bar 3%/5% (1021), bar1, bar2, stop0900 (arms-full-1103), removal tilt (1109), plus the four new arms. On about 30 days (research/overfit.py:29 MIN_OBS 30; 28 days were available on 9 Nov) a pass is unlikely.

Weak live support for the idea exists but is not by expected-CLV bin: top-ups closed -1.5% on 9 Nov and -1.2% on 10 Nov, horses at the 5 top-up cap -0.74% and -2.05% (ledger lines 634, 637, 652, 655).
checks.corrected_claim: On 10-20 Oct (11 days, the rule before the guard, ladder, max price 200 and cap of 5 top-ups) about 70% of the matched money (GBP29,114) went on fills with expected CLV of 3-6%, which closed between -1.1% and +1.2% after the cuts (ledger review-1020); this has not been measured for the current rule (22 Oct on). Since the 10:00 stop (5 Nov) the GBP4,000 day limit was reached on 1 of 6 live days (7 Nov, 09:30 UK), so the displacement mechanism that sank the 16 and 20 Oct bar tests (5% and 6% top-up bars, 6% bar, drift and short-price filters) mostly no longer applies, and no flat 4% or 5% bar has been replayed on the 10:00 window. But it is not true that every cut lost only through displacement: replay-nr-bar-1021, the rising-bar and 09:00-stop arms of arms-full-1103, and removal-tilt-replay-1109 (run on the 10:00 window with the limit not binding, GBP2,986 a day) all lost while staking less, because the money removed was net positive after the cuts. The prior for a higher bar is therefore weak to negative and the possible gain is small (the 3-3.5% bin was about -GBP33 over 11 days; the 4-6% bins were positive). Worth doing: the descriptive step only first - live fills 22 Oct - 10 Nov by expected-CLV bin x first back/top-up x reached-the-cap, CLV after the cuts. A replay of flat 4%/5% bars (all backs, top-ups only) is justified only if the 3-4% bin is clearly negative there; it must remove the hard-coded trade_from 06:15 in the replay_1108.py machinery (blend_ladder_replay_1020.py:51), be registered first, and count at least 14 prior and new bar/filter trials in the deflated Sharpe.
checks.already_tried: Bar and filter cuts already tested through the trader's code, all losing: stake-per-horse-1016 (5% top-up bar worse, limit spent later); blend-ladder-replay-1020 (top-ups at 6%+: GBP1,822 vs GBP2,131 live; blend+ladder+6% GBP1,851); rule-candidates-replay-1020 (bar 6% GBP1,587, no drift GBP2,227, short bar GBP2,255, 6%+no drift GBP1,188 vs GBP2,391); replay-nr-bar-1021 (3%/5% bar after expected cut: -GBP231 / -GBP182 on GBP3,078 / GBP8,365 less staked); arms-full-1103 (bar +1%/h GBP5,766, +2%/h GBP5,402, stop 09:00 GBP5,457, no top-ups GBP2,583, two top-ups GBP4,999 vs GBP6,101); removal-tilt-replay-1109 on the 10:00 window, limit not binding (skip low third: -GBP1,444.32, 90% interval -71.98 to -32.47 a day, ahead 6 of 28 days; "no further filter of this kind"). Descriptive no-redeploy read that pointed the other way: reductions-1021 (3% bar after expected cut keeps GBP8,632 at +11.9%, drops GBP30,737 at -0.43%: GBP1,027 vs GBP895, 10-21 Oct, not replayed). NOT tried: a flat 4% or 5% clv_bar (all backs or top-ups only) on the 05:15-10:00 window; the expected-CLV calibration table for fills after 20 Oct.

checks.reason:
Checked the finding's citations against reports/research_ledger.jsonl and TRADING.md. CONFIRMED: (a) ledger line 409 review-1020 calibration (3-3.5% -0.3% on GBP11,117 ... 25%+ +56.2%; "3-6% expected closes level, 70% of the money"); (b) line 410 rule-candidates-replay-1020 verdict (bar_6pct GBP1,587 vs GBP2,391, "last back 19:04: the money moves to later races"); (c) line 403 topups-1020 (under 6% GBP21,806 at -1.2%); (d) day stakes 5-10 Nov in TRADING.md lines 1707-1769 (3,934.82 / 2,942.70 / 3,999.99 / 2,474.27 / 2,074.63 / 1,789.84; limit reached only 7 Nov at 09:30 UK); (e) line 650 removal-tilt-replay-1109 "served rule averaged GBP2,986 a day ... what is on offer at the bar, not the limit or the selection, is what binds"; (f) trading/config_live.json clv_bar 0.03, trade_until 10:00, max_topups 5. No expected-CLV-bin calibration has been rerun since 20 Oct (grep of ledger lines 411-676, TRADING.md, reports/*.md, docs/*.md: none) - so the descriptive gap is real.

OVERSTATED: "lost only because the budget flowed to later races" is not what the wider record says. Three later tests lost where displacement was weak or absent: (1) replay-nr-bar-1021 (line 427): a uniformly higher bar lost GBP231 (3%) and GBP182 (5%) while staking GBP3,078 / GBP8,365 less and reaching the limit on 4 days not 9 - verdict "drops good backs with the bad"; (2) arms-full-1103 (line 569): rising bar bar1 GBP5,766 and bar2 GBP5,402 vs rule GBP6,101, stop0900 GBP5,457, 21 days; (3) removal-tilt-replay-1109 (line 650), run on config_live.json as it stands (05:15-10:00, limit not binding): dropping the lowest-edge third of markets lost GBP1,444.32 over 28 days (mean -GBP51.58 a day, 90% -71.98 to -32.47) because that money still closed positive (+1.46% at first crossing on GBP66,149, line 648) and was not redeployed; decision "no further filter of this kind". So the one test already run under the non-binding window says thin-edge money still adds pounds. Also the evidence base is stale in the finding's disfavour: the -1.2% top-up figure includes the 6th-20th top-ups (-3.3%, -4.7%) that max_topups 5 removed on 22 Oct, and the 10-20 Oct calibration mixes all hours to 21:30 (10:00 on closed about 0% after cuts on GBP14,518, window-1000 line 593; before 10:00 +5.5% after cuts on GBP88,110, live-by-hour-1104 line 592). The before-10:00 3-6% bin after cuts is not measured.

SIZE: by construction bets that close level are worth about zero to remove; gain exists only if the bin is negative. Recent stake averages GBP2,869 a day (the six days above sum to GBP17,216.25); even if 70% of it sat at -1% that is about GBP20 a day against a record of GBP197 a day (6,314.40 / 32, TRADING.md). Weak hints it could be negative on flat days: 9 Nov top-ups -1.5%, capped horses -0.7%; 10 Nov top-ups -1.2%, 28 capped horses GBP1,365.66 at -2.05% (TRADING.md lines 1755-1769) - but 6 Nov capped horses +13.96% (line 610). Power: paired daily differences in these replays have sd of roughly GBP60 (from the removal-tilt interval), so about 30 days cannot resolve a +GBP10-20 a day effect, and the deflated Sharpe must count the bar family already tried (bar_6pct, bar_6pct_no_drift, short_bar, nr-bar 3%/5%, bar1, bar2, stop0900 plus the 4 new arms) - a pass is unlikely.

CONSTRAINTS: not forbidden. A replay needs a ledger entry before the run and deflated Sharpe >= 0.95 with all trials counted; changing clv_bar in trading/config_live.json is a live change and needs the owner's yes. The removal-tilt decision ("no further filter of this kind") and CLAUDE.md's standing verdict that the levers are price-improving, not bet-cutting, weigh against opening another bar grid.

CHEAPEST DECISIVE NEXT STEP: step 1 only, as one descriptive research query, no rule fitted - rerun section D of research/queries/done/review_1020.py (line 143-145, the pd.cut on edge) on live fills before 10:00 UK, 22 Oct - 10 Nov, CLV after reduction factors (betfair_live_marks BSP, as live_by_hour_1104.py does), by expected-CLV bin x first back / top-up number, with a day-bootstrap interval per bin. If the 3-4% bin's interval includes or sits above zero, close the lead without a replay; register the 0.04 / 0.05 top-up-only bar replay only if a bin's 90% interval is wholly below zero.

title: The edge is a first-look, first-hours, thin-book, long-price edge: 66% of the result came from the 06:00 UK hour
claim: Over 10 Oct - 4 Nov the 06:00 UK hour alone made GBP+3,292 of the GBP+4,986 fill-level result at +10.5% CLV after cuts; later hours are +1% to +3% and from 10:00 nil. First backs run +11% to +17% on about GBP900 a day while top-ups run +2% to +8% on about GBP3,000; the 21+ price band is 16.8% of the money at +15.7% while under 5.0 is about 0% on 26-40% of the money.
evidence: Ledger live-by-hour-1104: before 10:00 GBP88,110 at +10.7% at the fill, +5.5% after cuts, GBP+4,831; by hour 06 +10.5% (GBP+3,292, 21 of 22 days up), 07 +2.8%, 08 +3.4%, 09 +1.1%, 10 -0.4%; fills sum GBP4,986.11. Ledger timing-1104: by time to off 12-18h 18.4%, 8-12h 9.3%, 4-8h 5.2%, 2-4h 1.2%; best back median GBP2.79 at 06, spread 25%. Ledger staking-1103: 19 Oct - 3 Nov GBP58,936 at +5.85%, 21+ band 16.8% of the money at +15.7%. Ledger liquidity-1020: best back over 20% above the second +33.8% (GBP629), spread over 50% +26.3%, GBP10-25 offered -1.8%. Ledger review-1020: under 3 and 3-5 about 0% CLV on 40% of the money. First backs v top-ups by day: TRADING.md lines 1311, 1367, 1416, 1454, 1473, 1492, 1510, 1535, 1556.
why_it_matters: The edge scales with how many stale first prices exist before the market forms, not with stake: timing-1104 puts the rule's capacity at about GBP5,000 a day and a 07:00 start at GBP98 a day against GBP228 (0.80 scale). Growth must come from more first looks (earlier hours, more markets), not from bigger stakes on the same horses.
test_design: Missing breakdown to run once (descriptive, no rule): live_orders 22 Oct - 10 Nov joined to betfair_live_marks (final BSP, reduction factors) and betfair_live_markets: a 3-way table of UK hour of fill (05,06,07,08,09) x fill number (1st, 2nd-3rd, 4th-6th) x price band (<3,3-5,5-8,8-13,13-21,21-50,50-200), with stake, CLV after cuts, result after 2%, 90% interval by race bootstrap. Output answers which cells carry negative CLV at current rule; cells with interval wholly below zero on GBP2,000+ become registered replay arms.

checks.reason:
Every headline number traces to its source, but two parts of the claim are selective and the inference drawn from it is contradicted by the same ledger.

CONFIRMED (read directly):

From 10:00 GBP14,518 at about 0%, GBP+155 (line 593, TRADING.md:1635-1636).
- Line 579 (timing-1104): time-to-off 18.4/9.3/5.2/1.2%, best back median GBP2.79 and spread 25% at 06, 07:00 start GBP98 v GBP228 at 0.80, capacity about GBP5,000 a day - all match (TRADING.md:1613-1626). These are replay figures (12 Oct-2 Nov, uncapped by hour), not live.
- Line 572 (staking-1103): 19 Oct-3 Nov GBP58,936 at +5.85%, 21+ band 16.8% at +15.7% (first-price band, CLV at Betfair's settled price: research/queries/done/staking_1103.py:38-41).
- Line 401 (liquidity-1020) and 409 (review-1020) figures match.
- TRADING.md lines 1311, 1367, 1416, 1454, 1473, 1492, 1510, 1535, 1556 match (first backs +10.7% to +17.4% on GBP786-1,252; top-ups +2.8% to +8.3% on GBP2,197-3,067). WHAT DOES NOT HOLD AS WRITTEN:
1. The first-back/top-up ranges are 9 chosen days (22, 24, 26, 28-31 Oct, 1-2 Nov), not the 10 Oct-4 Nov span. Left out: 15-17 Oct top-ups -0.9%, -8.9%, -4.6% (TRADING.md:972, 1016, 1075); 20 Oct +5.6%/-5.6% (1243); 21 Oct +24.4%/+0.3% (1275); 25 Oct +12.4%/+1.7% (1394); 3 Nov +4.8%/+0.1% (1593); 4 Nov +8.4%/-0.3% (ledger 594); 9 Nov +4.2%/-1.5% (634); 10 Nov +2.6%/-1.2% (652). 2. "Under 5.0 about 0% on 26-40% of the money": the about-0% reading is 30 Sep-20 Oct only (review-1020; longshots-1020 line 408: 42% at +0.5%). The 26% is one day's share, 19 Oct (TRADING.md:1226). The under-5.0 CLV under the rule since 21-22 Oct is not in the ledger: not measured.

And timing-1104 itself calls GBP1,000 to win "the one larger lever" (GBP298 v GBP272 a day; TRADING.md:1627-1629; paper-agents-rescore-1104b: +GBP21 a day at 0.80, capped by depth), while the earlier hours measured small: 05:15 start +GBP11 a day, evening before +GBP12 a day (line 579), evening arm "nothing to scale" (TRADING.md:1815-1817).

TEST DESIGN: feasible but one data error - betfair_live_marks has no reduction-factor columns (betfair_recorder.py:634-637 MARK_FIELDS); adjustment_factor and removal_utc are only in the raw books (BOOK_FIELDS, betfair_recorder.py:54-60), which is where live_by_hour_1104.py:42-64 reads them. It should be split at 5 Nov: the earlier replays' reason filters lose (money moves to later, worse bets under a binding limit: rule-candidates-replay-1020, line 410) does not apply when the limit is slack. 105 cells on about 20 days is a multiple-comparison risk.

The fixed closing weights (0.774 market / 0.263 model) sit on a relationship whose fitted weights moved from 0.47/0.50 to 0.66/0.32 between consecutive weeks.

Ledger changes-1109: first backs a median 3.3% over the BSP, expected +6.3%, realised +4.2%; changes-1106: 12.2% over, expected +6.2%. Ledger forecast-1022: expected GBP2,746.75 at the fill v settled CLV x stake GBP1,463.43 (0.53); last 7 days result/expected -0.01. Ledger closing-refit-replay-1109: a walk-forward refit of the blend lost (GBP-1,446.91 and GBP-938.51 over 28 days), so a naive refit is closed. why_it_matters: On low-margin days the rule stakes the same money for about nothing (14-21 Oct: 8 days, about GBP32,000 staked, flat). A day- or market-level state variable that scales the budget or the bar could remove the flat stretches without touching good days. Size not measured.
test_design: Descriptive pass, registered as such: for each live day 10 Oct - 10 Nov and each market at its first read, compute features known at that read - median |ln(best back / predicted BFSP)| across runners, book overround at best back, median spread, overnight matched money (books_overnight from 4 Nov), field size, minutes to off - against the market's realised first-back margin ln(price/BSP) after cuts. Fit nothing live; report rank correlation by day (walk-forward, each day scored on a fit of prior days). If out-of-day rank correlation of market-level margin is above 0.1 with its 90% interval above zero, register a replay arm that orders the day's budget by the forecast margin instead of time order. Pass rule as the ledger's (interval above zero, deflated Sharpe >= 0.95).

title: Taking the offer in a 25-200% spread book pays the whole spread: passive backs on rule horses were never tested and the stream record now allows it
claim: All live backs are FILL_OR_KILL at the price read on a 60-second poll, in books whose spread is 25% at 06:00 and about 196-209% at 05:00. Fills where a lone better price sat on top closed +33.8% and ladder first backs beat best-back first backs on most days, so price improvement is where the CLV is; yet the only resting-order test was two-sided quoting on every runner, which lost. A one-sided resting back on rule horses only has not been tried.
evidence: TRADING.md lines 294-297 (FILL_OR_KILL, nothing rests); trading/config_live.json poll_seconds 60. Ledger timing-1104 (spread 25% at 06, 12.5% at 08); night-before-1106 (day's books at 05 UK spread 1.96), night-before-1107 (2.09). Ledger liquidity-1020 (best back over 20% above the second +33.8% on GBP629; 10-20% +18.4%). Ladder first backs v best back: TRADING.md lines 1344 (+19.8 v +6.1), 1418 (+23.1 v +6.5), 1457 (+28.0 v +8.9), 1537 (+22.8 v +3.5). Ledger execution-audit-1021: 152 orders EXPIRED, GBP1,024 asked, CLV +13% at the price asked. Paper desk: quotes_model3 GBP-236, quotes_mid2 GBP-14,043 (TRADING.md lines 1656-1659); 'the horse books carry no traded ladder' (line 1681). CLAUDE.md: horse WIN Exchange Stream recorded beside the trader from 10 Nov (research.horse_stream_record).
why_it_matters: A resting back at, say, 10% above the best back that fills even a third of the time converts spread into CLV on the horses already selected; it also adds capacity in exactly the hours where depth is GBP2.79. Adverse selection (filled only when the horse drifts) is the risk. Size not measured.
test_design: Data: betfair_stream/horse/<day>/ (traded ladder and full book) from 10 Nov, 20+ days. For each horse at the minute the served rule first clears the bar: simulate a resting back of the rule's stake at best back x (1.05, 1.10, 1.20), capped below the best lay, queue position behind displayed size at that price, matched only by traded volume at or above that price in the next 15/30/60 minutes, the unfilled remainder taken at the then best back if still over the bar. Score CLV after reduction factors and result after 2% against taking at once, paired by horse, day-bootstrap. Register before the run; pass: positive daily difference with 90% interval above zero and deflated Sharpe >= 0.95 over the 9 arm cells; then a paper forward test - nothing live without the owner's yes.

title: After a withdrawal the 'never under the model's price' guard and the ladder still use the full-field predicted BFSP
claim: The closing model re-normalises the model's prices over the runners left (closing_inputs), but the owner's guard compares the best back with the raw 04:00 predicted_bfsp, and _ladder recovers that same raw price from d.move. Once a runner at model probability q is out, every other runner's true model price is about (1 - q) times shorter, so the guard is too strict by 1/(1 - q) and blocks backs the rule intends. Decision.move is documented as 'the model's price for the runners left' but is not.
evidence: trading/strategy.py:181 (over_model = log(back / model_price) with model_price the raw array), 194 (move = log(back / r.model_price)), docstring line 60; trading/session.py:326-329 (ladder: ours = d.price / exp(d.move)); model/race_book.py:88-89 (lq_model normalised within the race); TRADING.md:100-103 states the model is re-normalised over active runners; TRADING.md:506-508: withdrawals cut the settled price of 28% of the stake by 4% to 41% on 4 Oct.

test_design: Replay on recorded books (S3 betfair_live/<day>/books_trader, the day's predictions/<day>.csv, BSP from betfair_live_marks): for every poll 05:15-10:00 UK in races with a REMOVED runner, compute decisions with guard price = predicted_bfsp x sum(1/predicted_bfsp over ACTIVE)/sum(1/predicted_bfsp over all). title: The 04:00 run prices on a history that stops two days back: yesterday's results are not in the database when the card is priced
claim: daily-results.yml scrapes at 21:30 UTC with --to today, and scraper.py itself records that HRB has not published the day's results by then, so day D's results only enter the S3 database at 21:30 UTC on D+1. The 04:00 UTC prediction for D+1 (and the 00:10 evening run) therefore builds every feature on history to D-1 at best, while training built each day's features with the previous day's results present. No step in the serving path checks or repairs this.

Ledger confirms the lag in practice: card-as-table-check-1111 at 12:30 UTC on 11 Nov reads '10 Nov priced, results not yet loaded'. The serving QA (serving-feature-qa-1111) compared served card vs perfect card on the SAME history, so it cannot see this.
why_it_matters: Every recency feature is one day stale for every runner: trainer/jockey 14/30-day form, connection windows, Kalman ratings, form windows for horses that ran yesterday (days_since_lr=1 on the card but the run absent from fw_/fv_ windows - the Quick Returners population of the morning model). Size not measured. It is a pure train/serve skew, so any gain is free forecast accuracy on the 0.263 weight the closing model gives our price.
test_design: Ledger entry first. Read-only query on the full DB: for the 06:00 cards of 24 Oct - 9 Nov re-price each day twice with the served model and CARD_AS_TABLE=stall - (a) history to D-1 (as training), (b) history to D-2 (as served). Pass rule: (a) better than (b) by 2 se overall or in the days_since_lr<=2 subset. Then measure when HRB publishes: a probe that POSTs excelresults for D at 23:00, 01:00 and 03:00 UTC and logs row counts for a week. If results are up by 03:00 UTC, add a scrape step (scraper.py --from D-1 --to D-1 --no-backup, in memory, no S3 upload) before 'Run predictions' in predict.yml; owner's yes needed as it changes live prices.

title: DSLR1-4 and seven derived columns are broken under pandas 3: the day number is computed as days/1000
claim: custom_metrics.py turns race_date into a day count with astype(np.int64) // 10**9 // 86400, which assumes nanosecond datetimes. pandas 3 parses the database's text dates to datetime64[us], so the 'day number' is floor(days/1000) (20 for every date in 2026) and DSLR1-4 are 0 unless the two runs straddle 4 Oct 2024 or 9 Jan 2022. Twelve served columns carry this.
evidence: model/custom_metrics.py:837-858 (and the same expression, unused, at 2026). Reproduced in a scratch venv on pandas 3.1.1: pd.to_datetime(['2026-10-01','2026-10-20','2026-11-11','2024-09-30']) -> dtype datetime64[us]; the engine's expression gives [20, 20, 20, 19] against true day numbers [20727, 20746, 20768, 19996]; a read_sql TEXT column and the history+card concat are also datetime64[us]. The jobs run pandas 3: requirements.txt:7 and pyproject.toml:15 pin only 'pandas>=2.1.0', and TRADING.md:765 / betfair_recorder.py:719 record a pandas-3-only crash on 7 Oct 2026; the served model was trained through 2026-10-13 (bfsp_model_meta.json trained_through). Served columns: DSLR1, DSLR2, DSLR3, DSLR4, DSLR12diff, DSLR23diff, DSLR34diff, WgtDSLR, FinalDSLR, rDSLR, rw_FinalDSLR_z, rw_FinalDSLR_gap (meta feature_cols). Gain pattern fits a dead column: DSLR1 0.0022% of gain against days_since_lr_num 0.113%, whereas true exact copies split gain (OFS1 1.07% vs LR_ORR2 0.74%); ordering DSLR3 0.0285 > DSLR4 0.0165 > DSLR2 0.0144 > DSLR1 0.0022. No test covers DSLR (grep of tests/ finds none). Whether the 13 Oct training frame was itself built on pandas 3 is inferred, not confirmed.
why_it_matters: Twelve columns are noise or calendar-boundary flags today (0.118% of gain in total), and the horse's own gap pattern (run-to-run spacing, the one thing these were for) reaches the model only through HRB's single days_since_lr and the freshness block. The larger risk is the cause: unpinned '>=' dependencies on the live trader, so any library release can change served features between a training run and a 06:00 forecast with no test failing. P&L size: not measured.
test_design: 1) Confirm: in research-loop, load the cached matrix and print DSLR1.value_counts() and corr(DSLR1, days_since_lr_num); the bug predicts DSLR1 in {0,1} only. 2) Fix as a new drop-in block (engine not edited, per reports/bfsp_model_plan.md 'How the repairs are made'): gap_k = race_date.values.astype('datetime64[D]') differences for the last 4 runs, plus log gaps and the ratio last gap / median gap; evaluate_oos.py --feature-cache .feature_cache --blocks <new> --drop-features DSLR,WgtDSLR,FinalDSLR,rDSLR,rw_FinalDSLR with a placebo arm on the development window (never 2026-04-01 on). title: form_slope: debutants and one-run horses read exactly 0 ('flat form'), short histories are shrunk 4x, and the sign is inverted
claim: Beyond the audit's sign fault, the slope is computed with nansum over a fixed x grid: with no past runs the numerator is nansum of all-NaN = 0, so the slope is 0.0, not missing; with one run it is 0; with two runs the x values are not re-centred, so the slope is a quarter of the true two-point slope. A debutant, a once-raced horse and a truly steady horse are indistinguishable in form_slope_3/5, is_improving, is_declining, rFormSlope3 and rw_form_slope_3_z/gap.

title: More exact copies than the audit lists, and RPS is mostly field size
claim: RB is algebraically NFP ((N - p)/(N - 1) both ways), so EXP_RB3/5/10 = EXP_NFP3/5/10, rEXP_RB5 = rEXP_NFP5, RACE_RB = RACE_NFP, LR_RACE_RB = LR_RACE_NFP and FSARB = NFP x N / median(N); trainerjockeyWOA = trainerjockeyWAX and RACE_WOA follows. RPS (= racepacescore) is the SUM of expected early-position figures over the field, about 3 x field size, so it mostly repeats number_of_runners. draw_relative is -1/(N-1) for every jumps runner because the table stores stall 0 there.
evidence: model/custom_metrics.py:456-457 and 482-484 (NFP and RB formulas), 489 (FSARB), 1035-1050 (EXP_ loops over NFP and RB), 543 (WOA_raw = WAX_raw), 953, 963-972, 636 and 913 (sum, not mean), 1329-1342 with model/card_enrich.py:425-426 ('the table has 0 there' for jumps stalls; executed: pd.cut gives NaN for the negative value). Gain is split arbitrarily between twins, which makes importance tables misleading: rEXP_RB5 0.464% vs rEXP_NFP5 0.174%; OFS1 1.074% vs LR_ORR2 0.744%; rOFS3 0.997% vs rRWOLR3 0.888%; RPS 0.411% vs racepacescore 0.357% (bfsp_feature_importance.csv).
why_it_matters: No direct accuracy gain expected (trees are indifferent to copies), but with feature subsampling the copies raise the draw rate of the same signal and crowd out others, slow every fit, and make gain-based decisions (what to repair first) unreliable: the true weight of last-run N/BSP is 1.82%, of the PMW ranks more than any single row shows. Size: not measured.
test_design: Add these to the plan's batch F removal list. Check: sha256 of each pair's values on the cached matrix (as metric_audit.py does) must match before removal. Then one loop run with the copies withheld vs the served set: pass if the paired error change is within the placebo's noise and fit time falls; report the regrouped gain table (copies summed) to re-rank the repair batches.

checks.reason: Algebra holds (custom_metrics.py:456-457, 482-484) but RB and NFP are not bit-identical: a pure-Python check of (N-p)/(N-1) against 1-(p-1)/(N-1) for N 2-40 gives 532 of 819 cells equal, 287 off by 1.1e-16, so the proposed sha256 check will fail and ranks can break ties differently. WOA_raw = WAX_raw (543), sums at 636 and 913, EXP_ loops 1035-1050, draw_relative 1333 confirmed. Gains match the CSV (rEXP_RB5 0.464, rEXP_NFP5 0.174, OFS1 1.074, LR_ORR2 0.744, RPS 0.411, racepacescore 0.357). 'RPS is mostly field size': correlation not measured. FSARB is not itself served.
checks.corrected_claim: RB equals NFP up to floating rounding (not bit for bit), so the EXP_RB, RACE_RB, LR_RACE_RB and RB rank columns duplicate their NFP twins and trainerjockeyWOA/RACE_WOA duplicate WAX; verify with a tolerance (max abs difference under 1e-12), not sha256. RPS is a field sum of expected early-position figures; its correlation with number_of_runners is not measured. draw_relative is -1/(N-1) on jumps rows (0.008% of gain).

title: No golden-frame test guards the engine: a library change or a card-format change alters served features silently

title: jumps_form reads 'refused to settle', 'ran out a winner' and 'left in lead when leader fell' as non-completions - and iteration 117 is being read on it

title: time_figure: the going allowance is the meeting's own mean, so every meeting's figures are centred on zero and class is erased
claim: In model/blocks/time_figure.py the day's allowance is the plain mean of the same races' deviations from a class-blind standard (including the race being rated), and the race figure is -(dev - ga). Per meeting the figures therefore average zero in seconds per furlong whatever the quality of the card: a Group-race card and a Class 6 card rate the same, and with 2 rated races each race keeps only half its own deviation. The tf_ features (13 served) measure 'fast relative to the other races that day', not speed on one scale.

title: Kalman rating: unrated horses are based on a zero-polluted median_or, and first ratings fall back to 70 in every code
claim: performance_figure_lbs (the Kalman block's reading) takes an unrated horse's base from the table's median_or, which is the race median with unrated runners counted as 0. In a race with exactly half the field unrated the base is (0 + lowest rating)/2 (e.g. 40), with fewer than half unrated it is a rating from the bottom half of the rated runners. The same polluted column anchors a horse's first rating, and when it is 0 or missing in an all-unrated race the anchor is a flat 70 lb, about 40 lb below a jumps novice's level. form_windows.run_measures does this correctly (masks 0, median of rated runners), so kr_ and fw_perf disagree on the same run.
evidence: model/perf_figures.py:157-158 (base.where(base > 0, median_or)) before the masked race median at :159-162; model/blocks/kalman.py:97 (perf), :99-101 (anchor = median_or>0, else card median, else ANCHOR_FALLBACK), :42 (ANCHOR_FALLBACK = 70.0). median_or includes zeros: model/card_enrich.py:406-412 ('the median over every runner, unrated as 0 ... as the table has them'). Correct version: model/form_windows.py:129-131. Ledger matrix-live-parity-new-blocks (line 201): kr_rating mean 76.8 lb, kr_vs_or read on 0.748 of runners. Related known fault 4 (non-finisher rated as running to its mark, perf_figures.py:172) is in reports/bfsp_model_plan.md:155; this one is not listed.
why_it_matters: kr_rating, kr_z, kr_rank, kr_vs_max and kr_vs_or (7 served features) carry artefacts exactly where the price error is largest - maidens, novices, bumpers (error 0.52 against 0.36 in handicaps, quoted in model/blocks/debut_market.py:3-4). Size: not measured.
test_design: Read-only query: for runs with official_rating = 0, the distribution of median_or against the masked median of rated runners in the race; share of runs where they differ by more than 5 lb; share of first-seen horses anchored at exactly 70 by code. Fix in kalman_v2: base = OR>0, else masked race median (run_measures' rule), non-finisher = no reading, anchor fallback = the code's decayed mean rating from earlier days. Register, then quick recipe 11 folds with kr_ withheld; pass = interval below zero overall and in maiden/novice/bumper races, beyond the placebo move.

checks.reason: model/perf_figures.py:157-158 fills an unrated base from median_or before the masked race median at :159-162; median_or counts unrated as 0 (model/card_enrich.py:406-412, table convention). model/blocks/kalman.py:97 reads that figure, :99-101 anchor = median_or>0, else rated card median, else ANCHOR_FALLBACK 70.0 (:42). form_windows.py:129-131 masks 0 first, so kr_ and fw_perf differ. title: Sectionals: the live table is fetched 2.5 hours before the site's morning refresh, and a failed fetch silently serves the committed table (ends 20 Oct)
claim: The sc_ block is trained on a complete table (every run's sectional present from the day after), but the live path reads whatever the Blandford site holds at 04:00 UTC: the site refreshes at 06:30 and 13:30 UTC, so yesterday's afternoon and evening runs cannot be in the 04:00 file, and meeting files are rewritten as PDFs arrive. title: Spread cliff in market_now: a runner crossing lay/back 1.25 gains 5-7 points of expected CLV with no model disagreement, and the threshold sits at the 06:00 median spread
claim: model/race_book.py market_now reads the market as the geometric mid when lay/back <= 1.25 and as the bare back price otherwise. Inside one race that mixes both regimes, the wide-spread runner is read about 10% shorter than its neighbours, so its expected CLV jumps past the 3% bar by itself. The live trader's most valuable hour (06:00) has a median spread of 25%, so the rule is selecting on which side of an arbitrary constant a runner falls.

title: Expected CLV is taken from renormalised lognormal draws, which shifts the mean away from the fitted q_hat: about -1.5 points on favourites and +1.4 to +2.4 on outsiders, plus a fixed per-runner Monte Carlo offset
claim: fit_closing_model fits q_hat by cross-entropy, so q_hat is already the conditional mean of the closing probability. race_expected_clv then averages draws that are renormalised to the book after the -0.5 sigma^2 correction; renormalising breaks mean preservation, so E[draw] != q_hat. The live EV therefore contains a term that depends only on sigma (one constant, 0.347) and the runner's share of the book, not on any information.
evidence: model/race_book.py:164-173 (closing_draws: -0.5*sigma**2 then q/q.sum), :445-448 (EV = back x mean of draws). data/models/closing_model_novol.json: band_edges all 0.0, so every runner gets band_sigma[4] = 0.3470 whatever its price or time to the off. Arithmetic check (repo function, hypothetical books, model = market, NOT recorded data): 8 runners: draws EV [1.02, 0.97, 0.34, -0.54, -1.50, -2.96, -4.40, -6.57]% vs point EV back x book x q_hat - 1 = [2.69, 0.93, -0.56, -2.03, -3.34, -5.03, -6.69, -8.99]%; 14 runners: favourite 1.83% (draws) vs 3.33% (point), 116-shot -7.23% vs -8.67%. trading/strategy.py:173 seeds the draws by the sum of selection ids, so with clv_draws 20000 (trading/config_live.json) each runner carries a persistent offset of sd about 0.245 points (0.347/sqrt(20000), my arithmetic). Ledger closing-correction-1008: live bias 'longer prices drift more (+0.09-0.10 a log unit of price)', the direction in which this term overstates outsiders.
why_it_matters: Not measured on fills. The tilt (up to about 4 points between favourite and outsider) is larger than the 3% bar. Note the direction on favourites: removing the term alone would raise short-price EV by about 1.5-1.7 points, where live CLV has been about 0% (review-1020: under 3 and 3-5 about 0% on 40% of the money), so the fix must ship with a fitted price term (next finding), not alone. The draws stay for build_book's risk only.
test_design: On every 05:15-10:00 read in books_trader from 12 Oct: compute EV_draws (as served) and EV_point = back x book x q_hat - 1. Tabulate realised back/BSP - 1 after reductions by first-price band (under 3, 3-5, 5-8, 8-13, 13-21, 21+) against both. Pass rule for adopting the point form plus a one-parameter price term: lower mean absolute calibration error across the six bands walk-forward by day, and on the live ledger (fills the changed rule would drop or add at first crossing) a positive CLV x stake difference with a 90% day-bootstrap interval above zero. Register in reports/research_ledger.jsonl first; count it with the three closing-refit trials for the deflated Sharpe.

title: A horse can clear the bar with no overlay of its own: the model disliking the favourite lifts every other runner's expected CLV
claim: Because the closing model is a softmax over the race, a long model price on one runner (often the favourite) raises q_hat for all the others. Runners where our price equals the market's can then clear 3%, and the min_move guard (back >= raw predicted BFSP) lets them through at exactly zero own overlay. The edge on such 'field-induced' backs depends on the model being right about a horse we are not backing, which is where the feature faults (stale form, first-time fences) bite.
evidence: model/race_book.py:116-118 (softmax within race), trading/strategy.py:179-182 (guard on ln(back / model_price) with raw model_price). Arithmetic check (repo function, hypothetical 8-runner book, NOT recorded data): model 50% longer than market on the favourite only, equal elsewhere: other runners' EV [4.71, 4.09, 3.20, 2.22, 0.72, -0.78, -3.02]% - three clear the bar. Ledger review-1021: beginners' chases -21.1% (-26.1 to -11.7) on GBP1,535, 'the model's form from hurdles cannot read a horse's first fences'. Ledger topups-1020: top-up fills '15-35% over the predicted BFSP GBP15,515 at -3.7%; over 50% GBP4,188 at +20.7%' - own overlay matters.
why_it_matters: Not measured. If field-induced backs close near zero they are a clean, information-based cut (unlike a blanket higher bar), concentrated in short prices where the GBP200 cap puts the most money.
test_design: For every live first back 21 Oct - 10 Nov recompute from the logged p_model, p_market, best_back: own = 0.263 x (lq_model_i - lq_market_i) and field = EV - own (in log terms, from the softmax normaliser). Split first backs into terciles of own / (own + field). Table settled CLV x stake and money by tercile x price band. If the lowest-own tercile's CLV is below the highest's by a 90% race-bootstrap interval excluding zero and is itself not above zero, pre-register one rule: min_move raised from 0 to ln(1.05) on the normalised model price. title: Capacity is what binds: convert fill-or-kill takes into resting backs at the already-approved price, tested on the Exchange Stream record

title: The bar is gross: commission asymmetry is not in the expected CLV, and it costs about a tenth of the profit
claim: _plan_closing_clv compares gross expected CLV with clv_bar and never reads cfg.commission. Commission is charged on each market's net winnings and not rebated on losing markets, so a hedged position with a wide price-move distribution pays commission on its good outcomes only. On the record this has been about 10% of the profit before commission, not 2%.
evidence: trading/strategy.py:148-197 (no use of cfg.commission in the closing_clv plan); trading/config_live.json commission 0.02, clv_bar 0.03. Ledger review-1020: 'result GBP1,656 before and GBP1,494 after commission (GBP162)' over 21 days (9.8%, my division). Ledger hedge-ratio-1021: 'none: ... commission GBP979' vs about GBP500 hedged - commission scales with outcome spread. My arithmetic, not data: for a single position with mean 3% and sd 0.35, E[max(x,0)] is about 0.155, so 2% commission is about 0.3 points and 5% about 0.8 points of the 3% bar. research/expert_fee.py bands not applied here (CLAUDE.md: 'a fee on profit does not move the trader's bar').
why_it_matters: A 3% gross bar is roughly a 2.7% net bar at 2% and lower if the rate rises; marginal bets (the 3-3.5% band, GBP11,117 at -0.3% on 10-20 Oct, review-1020) are below break-even net. Small in pounds; not measured for the current era.
test_design: In the calibration query (finding 3) add a column: market-level commission actually charged, allocated to fills pro rata to positive CLV x stake. Report net CLV by EV band. If the 3-4% band's net is not above zero (90% interval), fold a net term into the bar: require EV - c x E[max(x,0)] >= bar using the draws already made (race_book.closing_draws gives the distribution; compute per race net of the positions held in that market). Scored inside finding 3's registered test, not as a separate trial.

title: Scrape write path: the file's own date is not checked, and the upsert can neither blank nor de-duplicate an amended result

title: The database is uploaded whole with no integrity, row-count or version guard, after steps that can be killed mid-write in WAL mode
claim: horse_racing.db is put in WAL mode by the scraper, two later load steps run under 'timeout' (SIGTERM mid-write), and the upload then overwrites the single S3 object with whatever the main file holds - no PRAGMA wal_checkpoint, no integrity_check, no check that race_results did not shrink, and the backup is called with versioned=False.
evidence: scraper.py:138 (PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL); .github/workflows/daily-results.yml:109-111 ('timeout 900 python betfair_prices.py ...') and :121 ('timeout 600 python betfair_recorder.py --load-db'); :141-150 upload conditioned only on steps.scrape.conclusion == 'success'; scripts/fetch_data.py:74-101 (plain s3.upload_file); scraper.py:706-707 (upload_db(versioned=False)); grep for 'integrity_check|wal_checkpoint' across *.py and *.yml: no hit. why_it_matters: One bad upload replaces 2.0m rows of history (reports/qa_review_2026-09-23.md:206: 2,004,155 runners) that take days of rate-limited scraping to rebuild; the Sept incident lost six months of nightly results through the same job. Probability: not measured; severity: the whole model.
test_design: Add to scripts/fetch_data.py --upload-db (test in tests/ with a temp DB): before upload run PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE); PRAGMA integrity_check must return 'ok'; SELECT COUNT(*), MAX(race_date) FROM race_results must be >= the values recorded at download (write them to a sidecar at --db-only time); upload first to horse_racing/<UTC date>.db (keep 14) then copy to horse_racing.db. Pass rule: a test that truncates race_results, or leaves a -wal file with uncheckpointed commits, makes the upload exit non-zero; a dry run on the real DB reports equal counts. Also confirm S3 bucket versioning is on (not checkable from the repo).

checks.reason: Confirmed: scraper.py:138 sets WAL; daily-results.yml:110 and :121 run the loads under timeout; upload :146 keyed only on the scrape; scripts/fetch_data.py:74-101 is a plain upload_file; no integrity_check or wal_checkpoint anywhere; betfair_recorder.py load_db has no SIGTERM handler (the one at :886 covers recording only). A load killed by timeout can leave committed pages in the -wal file; the main file alone is then uploaded unless a later step reopened and closed the database cleanly. title: Price-file archive and load: no content check on archived files, parse failures never retried, replaced rows never removed
claim: archive_published stores any 200 response that does not start with '<' and never refetches a name already in the archive once it is older than 7 days; load_files records a file that failed to parse as 'skipped' in betfair_prices_files, which pull_s3 treats as loaded forever; and a recent file re-loaded with INSERT OR REPLACE leaves behind rows Betfair removed in the rewrite. A truncated or wrong-day file therefore becomes a permanent hole.
evidence: betfair_prices.py:605-608 (only '<' test; download_day at :245 does check the EVENT_ID header), :660 (todo = not in have or recent), :411-417 (status 'skipped: ...' written), :745-746 and :755 (skipped files count as loaded), :419-421 (REPLACE by event_id, selection_id, market_type; no delete by source_file), :299 (race_date falls back to the file's date although 'a file holds the racing of the day before its name', ledger price-match-1009).
why_it_matters: The price files are the only source of MORNINGWAP, volumes and in-play extremes back to 2018 - the closing model's training data and every morning-edge backtest. Holes bias coverage by date silently. Number of bad files: not measured.
test_design: Queries: (1) SELECT status, COUNT(*), SUM(rows) FROM betfair_prices_files GROUP BY status - expect only 'loaded'; list every other. (2) Calendar: for each day 2018-01-01..yesterday expect dwbfpricesukwin/ukplace/irewin/ireplace rows in betfair_prices_files; list missing names and files with rows < 20 for ukwin. (3) SELECT source_file, COUNT(DISTINCT race_date) FROM betfair_prices GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT race_date)>2 (wrong-day content). (4) rows whose loaded_at is older than their source_file's latest loaded_at in betfair_prices_files (left behind by a rewrite) - expect 0. Fix: validate header + >= 1 data row before put_object; re-queue 'skipped' files and files failing (2); delete by source_file before insert. Pass: all four queries empty after one archive + load cycle.

checks.reason: Code read. betfair_prices.py:605-608 accepts any 200 body not starting with '<' (download_day :245 does test EVENT_ID). :658-660 todo = not in archive or within refresh_days (default 7, :625; 2 in live-record.yml:170). :411-417 writes 'skipped: ...'; :745-746 treats every betfair_prices_files row as loaded whatever its status (the table comment at :369 says this is by design). :364 UNIQUE(event_id, selection_id, market_type) with INSERT OR REPLACE and no delete by source_file. Overstated: a skipped file IS retried while inside the 7-day refresh window (:754-755); the :299 fallback only applies to rows whose EVENT_DT fails to parse. Bad-file count: not measured.
checks.corrected_claim: The archive stores any non-HTML 200 response and never refetches a file older than the refresh window (7 days; 2 in live-record.yml). A file that fails to parse is logged 'skipped' and is retried only while inside the 7-day refresh window, then counts as loaded for good. Re-loads replace by (event_id, selection_id, market_type) and never delete rows Betfair dropped. So a truncated or malformed back-filled file is a permanent, unreported hole. Number of such files: not measured.
checks.already_tried: No test of file status or calendar coverage found in the ledger. Same class of silent gap was found and fixed once: ledger price-match-1009 (re-load cleared race_results_id; fixed by match_days) and price-match-1010 (repaired, 99.8% matched). price-archive-inventory-1002 gives the expected count: UK/IE win and place 3,319 days each from 31 Aug 2017. coverage_report (betfair_prices.py:491) reports rows and match rate by month only, not missing days or skipped files.
checks.next_step: Run one read-only query on the nightly database: status counts from betfair_prices_files plus a calendar of missing or under-20-row ukwin day files from 2018, against the 3,319-day listing.
